claims.text: The driver's claim stands or falls on his having been at the pickup. Under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and only a cancellation after that free wait attracts the 5.00 SGD fee under POL-NS-22; under the Tribunal's arrival test the driver is at the pickup only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within the 50 m radius for a STANDARD pickup. The derived arrival check on the trace returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null — no fix falls in the window around the 15:42:00 arrival marker at all — so the arrival event is uncorroborated and the fee has no predicate. I disclose that the trace carrying that check is impaired at weight 0.6 (issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION).

Disclosure of impairment, as POL-GEN-02 requires: EV-GPS-05064 is IMPAIRED with weight_multiplier 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — one 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker (15:42:00), the entire free-wait window and the cancellation (15:49:00), with the fixes either side of it several hundred metres from the pickup. The rider does not present that artifact as clean evidence: it contains no fix that can corroborate the arrival or place the driver at the kerb during the wait, and its own weight caps any finding that rests on it.

The rider's account is unrebutted. He says he was standing at the pickup at Blk 33 the whole time and never saw the car; the trace carries no rider track at all (rider_track empty), so no artifact places him anywhere else, and the only platform evidence that the driver was at the kerb is the arrival button the driver pressed himself. Nor can the driver fill his own twelve minutes of silence with a traffic explanation: the sole artifact that could carry one, EV-ADVIS-05064-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact for either side. Nothing may be read into the impaired trace (0.6, GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION) in the driver's favour: POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence unless a rule says so, and no rule says so here.

I do not contest the contact obligation. The chat log and the trip record show two in-app messages (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and one in-app call placed at 15:45:10, all before the 15:49:00 cancellation, so POL-NS-23 is satisfied on this record. But POL-NS-23 is a necessary condition, not a substitute for the arrival: the driver's claim is not that he failed to reach the rider, it is that he waited at the pickup, and compliance with the contact rule cannot cure the uncorroborated arrival under POL-NS-21. Contact alone therefore does not move the 5.00 SGD to the driver.

If the judge concludes that the arrival cannot be established either way on this record, the answer is still not to pay the driver. POL-GEN-26 requires escalation, with the open question stated — was the driver at the pickup during the free-wait window? — and an escalated fee is held rather than collected, so the rider is not left carrying the charge in the meantime. POL-NS-24 cannot close that question on an on-demand trip: there is no scheduled pickup time, so no 'scheduled time plus 5 minutes' deadline exists to measure the driver against, and it is precisely the fact the impaired trace cannot carry (weight 0.6, GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION).

The vocabulary of POL-GEN-03 must be read against the filer, and the filer here is the driver. The 5.00 SGD has already moved off him and to the rider — refund_issued_sgd 5.0, payment_status REFUNDED, and the fee_reversed event of 2026-09-06 19:30 recording 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver. The driver now asks for it back. Because no fix corroborates his arrival and the rider's account stands unrebutted, his claim fails and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null. DRIVER_COMPENSATION or FULL_REFUND would move the 5.00 SGD back to the driver, and this record does not support either.

claims.text: The cancellation was made inside the free wait rule. This booking was on-demand — trip_record.scheduled_at is null — so under POL-NS-21, and the policy's own free_wait_starts rule, the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival and not from any schedule: trip_record.arrived_at is 2026-09-06T15:42:00+08:00, the derived free_wait block ends the window at 15:47:00, and the platform's own wait_timer_expired event fires at 15:47:05. The driver cancelled at 15:49:00 — 420 s after arrival, 120 s past the free wait. The precondition POL-NS-22 depends on (a cancellation after the free wait) is therefore satisfied on the trip record alone.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the platform's records, not on the driver's account. The chat log carries two in-app messages sent by the driver — MSG-05064-001 at 15:42:20 and MSG-05064-002 at 15:46:00 — and trip_record.in_app_calls carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 15:45:10 (unanswered, rang 25 s). All three contacts precede trip_record.cancelled_at at 15:49:00, which is exactly what the derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met value of true records. Nothing in the 5.00 SGD fee is voided under POL-NS-23.

The amount charged is exactly the fee the policy fixes, and POL-NS-22 makes it the driver's money. The ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD and total_charged 5.00 SGD, and the derived money block records fee_matches_policy true against policy_fee_sgd 5.00 under POL-NS-22. Because the driver cancelled after the free wait, POL-NS-22 transfers that fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel and directs a ruling of DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 charged.

The present state runs against the driver, which is why the correct outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and not NO_ACTION. The ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.0, and the trip record's events carry the fee_reversed entry at 2026-09-06T19:30:00+08:00 — 'SGD 5.00 refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review'. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and means only that the present state stands; the driver filed, and the money has already moved to the rider, so NO_ACTION would leave both the refund and the withholding in place and the driver would recover nothing. The ruling the record supports is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, moving the fee back to the driver.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider no route to this refund. That clause lets the rider cancel at no charge; the rider cancelled nothing — trip_record.status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, cancelled_by is DRIVER and cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_NO_SHOW, and the chat log contains no rider message at all. The clause's only triggering fact is a rider cancellation that never happened, so its deadline limb is never reached: the derived driver_deadline block says 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time', meaning no scheduled pickup time can be breached, and the rider's fee-free exit does not exist on these facts.

The GPS trace is impaired and I say so plainly. EV-GPS-05064 is graded status IMPAIRED with weight_multiplier 0.6 and the issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION: a single 720 s hole from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the entire waiting window and the cancellation, while the fixes on either side sit several hundred metres from the pickup. The trace's own arrival_check returns corroborated false with nearest_fix null, and rider_track is empty. I do not ask the Judge to draw anything from that trace. POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring a fact from missing or impaired evidence, so the 720 s hole cannot be read as proof that the driver was not at Block 33; and the facts the driver's case actually needs — the arrival marker and the platform's dependent events (rider_notified 15:42:04, wait_timer_started 15:42:05, wait_timer_expired 15:47:05), the two messages, the call, and the fee — are carried by EV-TRIP-05064, EV-CHAT-05064 and EV-FARE-05064, each at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) no deciding fact on this record is capped below 1.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) nothing is being inferred from an impaired artifact.

The AI can and should decide this case, and POL-NS-26 makes its ruling on a no-show final. The disputed value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so no elevated confidence is required; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider fraud_flags 0, driver fraud_flags 0), so the 0.95 bar POL-GEN-22 imposes where a flag exists is not engaged; and no safety indicator touches this record, so POL-GEN-21 does not divert it. The fee is fixed at 5.00 SGD and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

ruling.explanation: This case cannot be decided on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than paid to either party. The money at stake is the 5.00 SGD no-show fee (EV-FARE-05064: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 5.00; the platform's fee_reversed event of 2026-09-06 19:30:00 refunded it to the rider and withheld it from the driver). Under POL-NS-22 that fee stands only if the driver cancelled after the 5-minute free wait, and on this on-demand trip the free wait runs from the driver's arrival (POL-NS-21: free_wait_starts = trip_record.arrived_at, here 15:42:00, ending 15:47:00; cancellation 15:49:00). But the free-wait limb reads the driver's arrival, and the category's arrival test (POL-NS-21/arrival_test) settles whether the driver was at the pickup only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m for a STANDARD pickup. The GPS trace EV-GPS-05064 is impaired and I rely on it only as impaired: weight_multiplier 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, one 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that covers the arrival marker, the entire waiting window and the cancellation, with no fix at all in the arrival window (arrival_check corroborated = false, nearest_fix = null). The fix that would corroborate the arrival is absent over exactly the stretch the test covers, so the driver's presence at the pickup cannot be established. POL-GEN-26 requires escalation precisely where a fact a rule needs — 'when the driver arrived' — cannot be established on missing or impaired evidence, and POL-NS-26 makes a no-show ruling final subject to POL-GEN-26. Both sides' positions fail on that same undecided limb: the driver's claim for the 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22 → DRIVER_COMPENSATION) needs the free wait to hold, and the rider's position that the fee is void needs it to fail. An undecided limb supports neither, and I infer nothing from the absent fix, so neither the driver's claim nor a NO_ACTION dismissal of it is available. What is not in dispute on clean records: the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met (driver messages MSG-05064-001 at 15:42:20 and MSG-05064-002 at 15:46:00, in-app call at 15:45:10, all before the 15:49:00 cancellation), and the fee is exactly the policy 5.00 SGD, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit (contact was attempted) and no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arise, and no POL-NS-25 referral (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is absent). The open question for the reviewer is whether the driver was at Block 33, Jalan Bukit Merah, during the free-wait window from 15:42:00 to 15:47:00 on 2026-09-06; the rider's account and the missing traffic-data artifact (EV-ADVIS-05064-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, carrying no fact) may be weighed there.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this no-show fee cannot be finally decided from the record, so the case goes to a human reviewer and no money moves.

What the record settles. The booking was on-demand (no scheduled pickup time), so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The driver tapped arrived at 15:42:00, sent two in-app messages (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered, 25 s), then cancelled at 15:49:00 — 420 s after the arrival tap and 120 s past the free wait. On the platform's own records (EV-TRIP-05064, EV-CHAT-05064) the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met. The fee is 5.00 SGD and matches the POL-NS-22 figure (EV-FARE-05064: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00), and 5.00 SGD has already been refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (fee_reversed at 2026-09-06T19:30; payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.0). The disputed value is 5.00 SGD, with no fraud flag on either profile and no safety indicator, so POL-GEN-21 and the elevated POL-GEN-22 bar are not engaged.

What the record does not settle. Whether the driver was actually at Block 33. POL-NS-21's arrival test decides that from the GPS trace corroborating the arrival event within 50 m of a STANDARD pickup, and EV-GPS-05064 is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — a single 720 s hole from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole free-wait window and the cancellation, with the fixes either side several hundred metres from the pickup. The trace's own arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null, and rider_track is empty. Because the trace is impaired over exactly the stretch the arrival test reads, the arrival is undecided: it neither supports a fee that needs the driver to have waited at the pickup nor defeats one.

The driver's claims. The free-wait arithmetic (POL-NS-21) is accepted, but its start point — the arrival — is the very thing left undecided. The contact claim (POL-NS-23) is accepted. The claim that the fee is the driver's and that POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION is rejected: POL-NS-22 only carries the fee to the driver where the cancellation came after a free wait that began at an established arrival. The POL-GEN-03 claim that DRIVER_COMPENSATION is owed because the present state runs against the driver is rejected for the same reason — an undecided limb supports neither a payment to the driver nor a refund to the rider, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION would simply freeze a state no rule has yet validated. The POL-NS-24 claim is accepted (the rider cancelled nothing; status CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER), but it gives the rider no route either. The claim that no deciding fact falls below weight 1.0 fails: the arrival corroboration on which the fee depends is carried only by the 0.6-impaired trace, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at 0.6 and under POL-GEN-02(3) that artifact, its weight and its issue code are named, as here. The POL-GEN-22 / POL-NS-26 claim is accepted on value and flags, but POL-NS-26's finality is expressly 'subject to POL-GEN-26'.

The rider's claims. The corroboration claim (POL-NS-21/POL-NS-22) is accepted as to the impairment and leads to the undecided limb, not to a refund. The POL-GEN-02 disclosure claim is accepted. What is not settled, and why it decides the case. POL-NS-21's free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and the policy's arrival test treats the driver as at the pickup only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m. The only GPS trace, EV-GPS-05064, is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION: one 720-second hole from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the cancellation, with the nearest fixes several hundred metres from Block 33 and the trace's own arrival check returning no corroborating fix. That is precisely the stretch the arrival test reads, so the arrival is undecided — neither corroborated nor disproved. The arrival marker is a status the driver set; the platform events that follow (rider notified 15:42:04, wait timer 15:42:05) are triggered by it and do not independently place the car at the kerb.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the mechanics, and the record bears that out. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled pickup time. The platform's trip record shows the arrival marker at 15:42:00, the free-wait timer starting at 15:42:05 and expiring at 15:47:05, the driver's two in-app messages at 15:42:20 and 15:46:00 and one unanswered in-app call at 15:45:10, and the driver's cancellation at 15:49:00 (420 s after arrival). The fare ledger shows the 5.00 SGD fee charged at 15:49:04 and later reversed, with 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) is satisfied: both messages and the call precede the cancellation, so nothing is voided on that ground, and I accept the rider's point that contact does not by itself stand in for arrival.

Everything then turns on one fact: was the driver actually at the pickup? Under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and the category's own arrival test makes that out only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m of a STANDARD pickup. The only artifact that could corroborate it, EV-GPS-05064, is IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION: a single 720-second gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the cancellation. The arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null — there is no fix at all in the +/-120 s window around 15:42:00 — and the fixes either side of the gap sit several hundred metres from Block 33. So the arrival limb is undecided: it is not corroborated, but nothing in the gap proves the driver was absent either, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from missing or impaired evidence, so I draw nothing from the gap against the driver. Equally I cannot take the arrival from the trip record's arrival marker alone, or from the platform events that depend on it: that marker is the status the driver set, and the platform's dependent events inherit it, so neither stands in for the corroboration the test requires. The rider's account that he stood at Blk 33 and never saw the car is his own word, and no no-show clause makes a counterparty statement the test for arrival, so it does not decide the point either.

An undecided limb supports neither the payment the driver needs under POL-NS-22 nor the refund the rider needs. Because the fact the fee depends on — when the driver arrived and whether he was at the pickup — cannot be established on impaired evidence, POL-GEN-26 sends this case to a human reviewer and the disputed 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected or refunded. That disposes of the two money arguments. The driver's case (POL-NS-22 transfers the 5.00 SGD, and the present state runs against him so the answer is DRIVER_COMPENSATION rather than NO_ACTION) fails because its predicate — a cancellation after a free wait that ran from an established arrival — is exactly what the record cannot establish. The rider's case (the fee has no predicate, so his refund stands and the answer is NO_ACTION) fails for the symmetrical reason: NO_ACTION means the present state stands because the present state is right, which requires the fee to be void, which requires the arrival limb to fail, and it is undecided. I accept the rider's POL-GEN-26 claim and his disclosure of the trace's 0.6 impairment and GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, and I accept the driver's point that POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing here (the rider cancelled nothing; status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER; an on-demand trip has no scheduled deadline to breach) and that no elevated confidence is required (value 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag; no safety indicator). POL-NS-26 would ordinarily make an AI no-show ruling final, but POL-NS-26 is expressly subject to POL-GEN-26, so the escalation stands.

No referral is added: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes (so no fee-amount referral), POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire, and POL-NS-25 does not fire (the rider's repeat no-show counter is absent). The open question for the reviewer — whether the driver was at Block 33 during the wait — belongs here rather than in referrals.

My confidence is 0.6, capped by the weight of the only artifact carrying the deciding fact, the impaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-05064, weight 0.6).
